title: Hector Berlioz's birth chart
metaDescription: Hector Berlioz's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.6° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Venus and Saturn sit 0.3° from an exact square — near enough that the tradition reads taste and structure as a single working part. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Sagittarius, but precisely: 18.6°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Mars in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 14.3° Sagittarius, Venus was at 2.9° Capricorn, Mars was at 17.7° Sagittarius. Read together: a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Venus at right angles from Saturn, 0.3° off exact. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Mars at 0.9°, and Mercury sextile Uranus at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. The Moon in Scorpio at 18.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mercury in Sagittarius at 14.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 2.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 fire, 3 water, 3 air, 1 earth by element and 4 mutable, 4 cardinal, 2 fixed by mode. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. All ten bodies ran direct that day — a chart with no apparent reversals anywhere in it.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.1° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 18.0°.
